readings.title: The Centrality of the Altar
readings.subtitle: Prohibition Against Sacrificing in the Open Field
readings.text:
[Leviticus 17:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[2] <dq>“Speak to Aharon, to <dn>את</dn> his sons, and to all the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded, saying,</dq>
[3] <dq>“Any man from the house of Yisra’ěl who slays a bull or a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slays it outside the camp,</dq>
[4] <dq>and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Appointment, to bring an offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, blood-guilt is reckoned to that man. He has shed blood, and that man shall be cut off from among his people,</dq>
[5] <dq>in order that the children of Yisra’ěl bring <dn>את</dn> their slaughterings which they slaughter in the open field. And they shall bring them to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at the door of the Tent of Appointment, to the priest, and slaughter <dn>את</dn> them as slaughterings of peace offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[6] <dq>“And the priest shall sprinkle <dn>את</dn> the blood on the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at the door of the Tent of Appointment, and shall burn the fat for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And let them no longer slaughter <dn>את</dn> their slaughterings to demons, after whom they whored. This is a law forever for them throughout their generations.” ’</dq>
[8] <dq>“And say to them, ‘Any man of the house of Yisra’ěl, or of the strangers who sojourn among you, who offers an ascending offering or slaughtering,</dq>
[9] <dq>and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Appointment, to do <dn>את</dn> it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that man shall be cut off from among his people.</dq>

readings.title: The Life is in the Blood
readings.subtitle: Prohibition Against Eating Blood
readings.text:
[Leviticus 17:10] <dq>‘And any man of the house of Yisra’ěl, or of the strangers who sojourn among you, who eats any blood, <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>My</dn> face against that being who eats <dn>את</dn> blood, and shall cut <dn>את</dn> him off from among his people.</dq>
[11] <dq>‘For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and <dn>I</dn> have given it to you upon the slaughter-place to make atonement for your lives, for it is the blood that makes atonement for the life.’</dq>
[12] <dq>“Therefore <dn>I</dn> said to the children of Yisra’ěl, ‘No being among you eats blood, nor does any stranger who sojourns among you eat blood.’</dq>
[13] <dq>“And any man from the children of Yisra’ěl, or from the strangers who sojourn among you, who hunts and catches any beast or bird, which is eaten, shall pour out <dn>את</dn> its blood and cover it with dust,</dq>
[14] <dq>for it is the life of all flesh. Its blood is for its life. And <dn>I</dn> said to the children of Yisra’ěl, ‘Do not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone eating it is cut off.’</dq>
[15] <dq>“And any being who eats a carcass or what was torn by a beast, be he a native or a stranger, he shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening. Then he shall be clean.</dq>
[16] <dq>“And if he does not wash or bathe his body, then he shall bear his crookedness.”</dq>

readings.title: Uncovering Nakedness
readings.subtitle: Prohibitions of Incestuous Relations
readings.text:
[Leviticus 18:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[3] <dq>‘Do not do as they do in the land of Mitsrayim, where you dwelt. And do not do as they do in the land of Kena‛an, where <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> you, and do not walk in their laws.</dq>
[4] <dq>‘Do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws, to walk in them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[5] <dq>‘And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, which a man does <dn>את</dn> and lives by them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[6] <dq>‘No one is to approach anyone of his own flesh to uncover his nakedness. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[7] <dq>‘The nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother you do not uncover. She is your mother, you do not uncover her nakedness.</dq>
[8] <dq>‘The nakedness of your father’s wife you do not uncover, it is your father’s nakedness.</dq>
[9] <dq>‘The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father, or the daughter of your mother, whether born at home or elsewhere, their nakedness you do not uncover.</dq>
[10] <dq>‘The nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, their nakedness you do not uncover, for theirs is your own nakedness.</dq>
[11] <dq>‘The nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, brought forth by your father, she is your sister, you do not uncover her nakedness.</dq>
[12] <dq>‘The nakedness of your father’s sister you do not uncover, she is your father’s flesh.</dq>
[13] <dq>‘The nakedness of your mother’s sister you do not uncover, for she is your mother’s flesh.</dq>
[14] <dq>‘The nakedness of your father’s brother you do not uncover, you do not approach his wife, she is your aunt.</dq>
[15] <dq>‘The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you do not uncover, she is your son’s wife, you do not uncover her nakedness.</dq>
[16] <dq>‘The nakedness of your brother’s wife you do not uncover, it is your brother’s nakedness.</dq>
[17] <dq>‘The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you do not uncover, nor do you take <dn>את</dn> her son’s daughter or <dn>את</dn> her daughter’s daughter, to uncover her nakedness. They are her relatives – it is wickedness.</dq>
[18] <dq>‘And do not take a woman as a rival to her sister, to uncover her nakedness while the other is alive.</dq>

readings.title: Abominations of the Nations
readings.subtitle: Prohibitions Against Molech, Homosexuality, and Bestiality
readings.text:
[Leviticus 18:19] <dq>‘And do not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness in her monthly separation of uncleanness.</dq>
[20] <dq>‘And do not have intercourse with the wife of your neighbour, to defile yourself with her.</dq>
[21] <dq>‘And do not give any of your offspring to pass through to Moleḵ. And do not profane <dn>את</dn> the Name of your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[22] <dq>‘And do not lie with <dn>את</dn> a male as with a woman, it is an abomination.</dq>
[23] <dq>‘And do not have intercourse with any beast, to defile yourself with it. And a woman does not stand before a beast to mate with it, it is a perversion.</dq>
[24] <dq>‘Do not defile yourselves with all these, for by all these the nations are defiled, which <dn>I</dn> am driving out before you.</dq>
[25] <dq>‘Thus the land became defiled, therefore <dn>I</dn> punished it for its crookedness, and the land vomited out <dn>את</dn> its inhabitants.</dq>
[26] <dq>‘But you, you shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and not do any of these abominations, the native nor stranger who sojourns among you,</dq>
[27] <dq>because the men of the land who were before you have done <dn>את</dn> all these abominations, and thus the land became defiled,</dq>
[28] <dq>‘So let not the land vomit <dn>את</dn> you out for defiling <dn>את</dn> it, as it vomited out <dn>את</dn> the nations that were before you.</dq>
[29] <dq>‘For whoever does any of these abominations, those beings who do them shall be cut off from among their people.</dq>
[30] <dq>‘And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Charge, so as not to do any of these abominable laws which were done before you, so as not to defile yourselves by them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Revering the Creator
readings.subtitle: Sabbaths, Idolatry, and Peace Offerings
readings.text:
[Leviticus 19:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying,
[2] <dq>“Speak to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘Be set-apart, for <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> am set-apart.</dq>
[3] <dq>‘Each one of you should fear his mother and his father, and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[4] <dq>‘Do not turn to idols, and do not make for yourselves moulded mighty ones. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[5] <dq>‘And when you slaughter a slaughtering of peace offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, slaughter it for your acceptance.</dq>
[6] <dq>‘It is eaten the same day you slaughter it, and on the next day. And that which is left on the third day is burned with fire.</dq>
[7] <dq>‘So if it is eaten at all on the third day, it is abominable, it is not accepted,</dq>
[8] <dq>and he who eats it bears his crookedness, because he has profaned <dn>את</dn> the set-apart offering of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and that being shall be cut off from his people.</dq>

readings.title: Restorative Justice and Equity
readings.subtitle: Gleaning, Honesty, and Loving the Neighbour
readings.text:
[Leviticus 19:9] <dq>‘And when you reap <dn>את</dn> the harvest of your land, do not completely reap the corners of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.</dq>
[10] <dq>‘And do not glean your vineyard or gather every grape of your vineyard, leave <dn>את</dn> them for the poor and the stranger. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[11] <dq>‘Do not steal, do not lie, do not deceive one another.</dq>
[12] <dq>‘And do not swear falsely by <dn>My</dn> Name and so profane <dn>את</dn> the Name of your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[13] <dq>‘Do not oppress <dn>את</dn> your neighbour or rob him. The wages of him who is hired is not to remain with <dn>את</dn> you all night until morning.</dq>
[14] <dq>‘Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling-block before the blind, but fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[15] <dq>‘Do no unrighteousness in right-ruling. Do not be partial to the poor or favour the face of the great, but rightly rule your neighbour in righteousness.</dq>
[16] <dq>‘Do not go slandering among your people. Do not stand against the blood of your neighbour. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[17] <dq>‘Do not hate <dn>את</dn> your brother in your heart. Reprove <dn>את</dn> your neighbour, for certain, and bear no sin because of him.</dq>
[18] <dq>‘Do not take vengeance or bear a grudge against <dn>את</dn> the children of your people. And you shall love your neighbour as yourself. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Statutes of Separation
readings.subtitle: Mixed Seeds, Guilt Offerings, and First Fruits
readings.text:
[Leviticus 19:19] <dq>‘Guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws. Do not let your livestock mate with another kind. Do not sow your field with mixed seed. And do not put a garment woven of two sorts of thread upon you.</dq>
[20] <dq>‘And when a man has intercourse with <dn>את</dn> a woman who is a female servant, engaged to a man, and to be ransomed, but she has not been ransomed nor set free, there should be an inquiry. But they are not put to death, because she was not free.</dq>
[21] <dq>‘And he shall bring <dn>את</dn> his guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, a ram as a guilt offering.</dq>
[22] <dq>‘And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his sin which he has done. And the sin which he has sinned shall be forgiven him.</dq>
[23] <dq>‘And when you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall reckon <dn>את</dn> their fruit as uncircumcised. For three years it is as uncircumcised to you, it is not eaten.</dq>
[24] <dq>‘And in the fourth year all its fruit is set-apart – praises to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[25] <dq>‘And in the fifth year you eat <dn>את</dn> its fruit, so that it increases its yield to you. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Rejecting Pagan Practices
readings.subtitle: Divination, Tattoos, and Mediums
readings.text:
[Leviticus 19:26] <dq>‘Do not eat meat with the blood. Do not practise divination or magic.</dq>
[27] <dq>‘Do not round the corner of your head, nor destroy <dn>את</dn> the corner of your beard.</dq>
[28] <dq>‘And do not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor put tattoo marks on you. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[29] <dq>‘Do not profane <dn>את</dn> your daughter by making her a whore, so that the land does not whore, and the land becomes filled with wickedness.</dq>
[30] <dq>‘Guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Sabbaths and reverence <dn>My</dn> set-apart place. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[31] <dq>‘Do not turn to mediums, and do not seek after spiritists to be defiled by them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[32] <dq>‘Rise up before the grey-headed. And you shall favour the face of an old man, and shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[33] <dq>‘And when a stranger sojourns with <dn>את</dn> you in your land, do not oppress <dn>את</dn> him.</dq>
[34] <dq>‘Let the stranger who dwells among <dn>את</dn> you be to you as the native among you, and you shall love him as yourself. For you were strangers in the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[35] <dq>‘Do no unrighteousness in right-ruling, in measurement of length, in weight, or in measuring liquids.</dq>
[36] <dq>‘Have right scales, right weights, a right ěphah, and a right hin. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim.</dq>
[37] <dq>‘And you shall guard <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and do <dn>את</dn> them. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>
